observation.visible_scene: A night view through a wet glass pane covered with running water streaks and scattered droplets. Against a black background, a roughly horizontal row of out-of-focus coloured bokeh circles (red, amber/yellow, white, green) is seen through the glass; the circles sit at mostly fixed screen positions while the water on the pane moves in front of them.
visible_changes: Vertical water rivulets and droplets flow and reshape continuously across the glass, appearing, merging, thinning and shifting downward over the excerpt.

The coloured bokeh dots keep their horizontal positions but cycle in hue and intensity: an amber dot on the left-centre turns red then yellow again, a dot among the right-hand reds flashes amber then back to red, and the central white pair dims toward pink and re-brightens.
The two white bokeh blobs drift leftward across the frame relative to the otherwise stationary coloured dots.
When water passes over a dot it deforms into a ring/donut shape rather than a solid disc.
The dark background and the row of coloured dots persist throughout without entering or leaving the frame.
outside_clip_unknowns: The real identity of the lights (traffic signals, vehicle lamps, street lights) and what causes their colour changes.
Whether the leftward-moving white blobs are a passing vehicle or a water-induced distortion.
Rain intensity and scene state before the first frame and after the last.
uncertain_details: Camera motion is uncertain but the coloured dots do not translate, so the view is treated as essentially static with only the water and the white blobs moving.
Colour cycling of a dot could be a genuine signal change or refraction through flowing water; the clip alone cannot separate the two.
Exact trajectory of the white blobs is hard to track because they overlap and deform under the rivulets.
